## Background

Quick comparison of selected analytes measured during SuRGE, the two most recent NLA campaigns (NLA17 and NLA22), lagos, and aquamatch (doc and chla).

## Data

Required data are created via the targets pipeline. Load data here.

```{r data, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
tar_load(dat_raw)
tar_load(lagos_chem)
tar_load(aquamatch_data)
tar_load(usgs_chem)
tar_load(usgs_chla)
tar_load(williamson_doc)
tar_load(usace_chem)
dat_lagos <- left_join(lagos_chem, dat_raw, relationship = "many-to-many")
dat_aquamatch <- left_join(aquamatch_data, dat_raw, by = "lake_id", relationship = "many-to-many")
dat_usgs_chla <- left_join(usgs_chla, dat_raw, relationship = "many-to-many")
dat_usgs_chem <- left_join(usgs_chem, dat_raw, relationship = "many-to-many")
dat_williamson_doc <- left_join(williamson_doc, dat_raw, relationship = "many-to-many")
dat_usace_chem <- left_join(usace_chem, dat_raw, relationship = "many-to-many")
acton_lake <- read_csv("input_data/external_data/ActonLakeIntegrated.csv") %>% clean_names()

```


## Extraction based chlorophyll a
We are missing extraction-based chlorophyll a measurements for `r dat_raw %>% filter(is.na(chla_lab_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` SuRGE lakes (mostly 2016 lakes). `r dat_raw %>% filter(is.na(chla_lab_shallow) & (!is.na(nla17_chla) | !is.na(nla22_chla)) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` of these lakes have chla estimates from 2017 and/or 2022 NLA, `r dat_lagos %>% filter(is.na(chla_lab_shallow) & (!is.na(lagos_chla_shallow)) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` of these lakes have chla estimates from LAGOS, `r dat_aquamatch %>% filter(is.na(chla_lab_shallow) & (!is.na(aquamatch_chla_shallow)) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` of these lakes has chla from aquamatch, `r dat_usgs_chla %>% filter(is.na(chla_lab_shallow) & (!is.na(usgs_chla_lab_shallow)) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` of these lakes have data from USGS, and  `r dat_usace_chem %>% filter(is.na(chla_lab_shallow) & (!is.na(usace_chla_shallow)) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` have USACE data. 

As expected, the concurrence among the various datasets is not great.

### Temporal variation
The LAGOS and aquamatch data highlight the temporal variation within a lake ( time series available for most lakes, hover cursor over point to reveal sample date). Long-term monitoring at Acton Lake and Cave Run shows the within-season temporal variation even more clearly. Chlorophyll a typically ranges from <10 to >100 between June and September each year in Acton Lake, which is a very broad range of values! Which value do CH4 emission rates correspond to most closely? Is it important that we match by sampling date, or is the seasonal average chla value a better indicator of CH4 production? Methanogens are likely responding to the longer-term process of algal senesence and settling to the bethos, rather than chla in the water column on any given day.

Cave Run, a large oligotrophic reservoir in KY, also shows within season variation, although not as extreme as Acton Lake. Despite the temporal variation in these data, a random sample from each lake will nearly always result in larger chl values for Acton relative to Cave Run. Maybe this is sufficient for our purposes. I expect the CH4 ~ chla relationship to be driven by end members along the trophic gradient, with lots of variation in between. 

I propose that we use chla measured on the day of SuRGE sampling when available, otherwise we aggregate whatever data are available.

```{r chla_time_series, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
{acton_lake %>%
    mutate(month = format(date, "%m")) %>%
    filter(month %in% c("06", "07", "08", "09")) %>%
 ggplot(aes(date, chlorophyll_a_ug_l)) +
    geom_point() +
    ggtitle("Acton Lake, small eutrophic")
} %>%
  ggplotly()

{usace_chem %>%
    mutate(month = format(usace_chla_shallow_sample_date, "%m")) %>%
    filter(
      month %in% c("06", "07", "08", "09"),
      lake_id == 1010, # closes to SuRGE index site
      !is.na(usace_chla_shallow)
    ) %>% 
    ggplot(aes(usace_chla_shallow_sample_date, usace_chla_shallow)) +
      geom_point() +
    ggtitle("Cave Run, large oligotrophic")
    } %>%
  ggplotly()
```

### Missing data sources
None of the datasets have chla from the same year as the SuRGE sampling.  

We expect to obtain additional monitoring data for the USACE lakes.

I found data for Acton Lake (lake_id == 1001) from Vanni's EDI repo.

Local Water District for BeaverCreek (lake_id == 204):
2024-08-14, chla = 8.12 ug/L

Williamson, T. J. (2020). A multi-scale approach to understanding how environmental variability modulates structure and function in reservoir ecosystems [Doctoral dissertation, Miami University]. OhioLINK Electronic Theses and Dissertations Center. http://rave.ohiolink.edu/etdc/view?acc_num=miami1595521238756147  

Burr Oak (lake_id == 1007), surge sampling on 6/21/2016:

2016-07-16: 23.65, 34.45, 27.70, 10.10, 13.20, 7.50

2016-07-23: 47.10, 50.05, 32.85, 22.50, 31.90, 28.50


```{r chla_table, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
left_join(
  # dat_raw + dat_lagos
  dat_raw %>% 
    select(lake_id, visit, sample_start, 
           chla_lab_shallow, nla17_chla, nla22_chla) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    filter(
      is.na(chla_lab_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)
    ) %>%
    select(-visit),
  dat_lagos %>% 
    select(lake_id, sample_date, lagos_chla_shallow) %>%
    rename(lagos_sample_date = sample_date)
) %>%
  left_join(
    # ... + aquamatch
    dat_aquamatch %>%
      filter(!is.na(aquamatch_chla_shallow)) %>%
      select(lake_id, activity_start_date, aquamatch_chla_shallow) %>%
      rename(aquamatch_sample_date = activity_start_date) %>%
      distinct()
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    # USGS data
    usgs_chla
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    # USACE data
    dat_usace_chem %>%
      select(lake_id, usace_chla_shallow_sample_date, usace_chla_shallow) %>%
      distinct()
  ) %>%
  rename(surge_sample_date = sample_start) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(lagos_chla_shallow) | 
      !is.na(aquamatch_chla_shallow) | 
      !is.na(nla17_chla) | 
      !is.na(nla22_chla) |
      !is.na(usgs_chla_lab_shallow) |
      !is.na(usace_chla_shallow)
  ) %>%
  select(-chla_lab_shallow, -usgs_chla_lab_shallow_units) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(lake_id, contains("date"))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sample_date = case_when(
      name == "nla17_chla" ~ as.Date("2017-01-01"),
      name == "nla22_chla" ~ as.Date("2022-01-01"),
      name == "lagos_chla_shallow" ~ lagos_sample_date,
      name == "aquamatch_chla_shallow" ~ aquamatch_sample_date,
      name == "usgs_chla_lab_shallow" ~ usgs_chla_lab_sample_date,
      name == "usace_chla_shallow" ~ usace_chla_shallow_sample_date,
      TRUE ~ as.Date("1789-07-14")
    ),
    source = case_when(
      name == "nla17_chla" ~ "NLA17",
      name == "nla22_chla" ~ "NLA22",
      name == "lagos_chla_shallow" ~ "lagos",
      name == "aquamatch_chla_shallow" ~ "aquamatch",
      name == "usgs_chla_lab_shallow" ~ "usgs",
      name == "usace_chla_shallow" ~ "USACE",
      TRUE ~ "Gandalf"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
  select(lake_id, surge_sample_date, source, value, sample_date) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  bind_rows(
    tribble(~lake_id, ~surge_sample_date, ~source, ~value, ~sample_date,
            204,  as.Date("2020-07-27"),  "Ohio Div. of Wildlife", 
            8.12, as.Date("2024-08-14"))
  ) %>%
  arrange(lake_id, source, sample_date) %>% 
  kableExtra::kable(caption = "Table 3. NLA, LAGOS, USGS, and aquamatch chla data for missing lakes") %>% 
  column_spec(1, bold = T) %>%
  kable_styling("hover", full_width = FALSE) %>%
  collapse_rows(columns = c(1:2)) 

```

## SO4
Sulfate wasn't measured until 2021 and we are missing data for `r dat_raw %>% filter(is.na(so4_shallow)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` SuRGE lakes. `r dat_raw %>% filter(is.na(so4_shallow) & (!is.na(nla17_sulfate) | !is.na(nla22_sulfate))) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` of these lakes have sulfate estimates from 2017 and/or 2022 NLA, `r dat_lagos %>% filter(is.na(so4_shallow) & (!is.na(lagos_so4_shallow))) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` of these lakes have sulfate estimates from LAGOS, `r dat_usgs_chem %>% filter(is.na(so4_shallow) & (!is.na(usgs_so4_shallow))) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` have estimates from USGS, and `r dat_usace_chem %>% filter(is.na(so4_shallow) & (!is.na(usace_so4_shallow)) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` have USACE data.


Comparison of SuRGE and NLA sulfate measurements is actually pretty good. Interestingly, most of the outliers in the plot below are in New Mexico South Dakota. I double checked the NLA and SuRGE data for these sites and don't see any issues. The New Mexico data shown are the mean of visits 1 and 2, which had very similar results. NLA sampled NLA22_NM-10013 in 2017 and 2022 with very similar results (data shown, 243 vs 83). 

Comparison with LAGOS is also pretty good. Again, the time series is useful for visualizing temporal variation.

The table shows the available data for the missing observations. A few lakes have observations over multiple years and these show pretty good agreement. I think we can impute the missing SO4 using these extrnal data sources (USGS, NLA, LAGOS, USACE, literature, personal communications).

Leslie and Lyons (2013) for sulfate:
Alum Lake (lake_id == 1002), summer 2010 and 2011: 0.55 mM = 52.8 mg/l

Local Water District for BeaverCreek (lake_id == 204):
2024-08-14, SO4 = 22.9 mg/L



```{r so4_table, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE}
full_join(
  # dat_raw and dat_lagos
  dat_raw %>% 
    filter(
      is.na(so4_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1) & (!is.na(nla17_sulfate) | !is.na(nla22_sulfate))
    ) %>% 
    distinct(
      lake_id, sample_start, nla17_sulfate, nla22_sulfate
    ) %>% 
    rename(
      SuRGE_sample_date = sample_start, 
      NLA17_SO4 = nla17_sulfate, 
      NLA22_SO4 = nla22_sulfate
    ), 
  dat_lagos %>% 
    filter(
      is.na(so4_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1) & !is.na(lagos_so4_shallow)
    ) %>% 
    select(
      lake_id, sample_start, sample_date, lagos_so4_shallow
    ) %>% 
    distinct() %>% 
    rename(
      SuRGE_sample_date = sample_start, 
      lagos_sample_date = sample_date)
) %>% # close full_join
  full_join(
    dat_usgs_chem %>%
      filter(
        is.na(so4_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1) & !is.na(usgs_so4_shallow)
      ) %>% 
      select(
        lake_id, sample_start, usgs_so4_shallow_sample_date, usgs_so4_shallow
      ) %>% 
      distinct() %>% 
      rename(
        SuRGE_sample_date = sample_start)
  ) %>%
  full_join(
    dat_usace_chem %>%
      filter(
        is.na(so4_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1) & !is.na(usace_so4_shallow)
      ) %>% 
      select(
        lake_id, sample_start, usace_so4_shallow_sample_date, usace_so4_shallow
      ) %>% 
      distinct() %>% 
      rename(
        SuRGE_sample_date = sample_start),
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(lake_id, contains("date"))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sample_date = case_when(
      name == "NLA17_SO4" ~ as.Date("2017-01-01"),
      name == "NLA22_SO4" ~ as.Date("2022-01-01"),
      name == "lagos_so4_shallow" ~ lagos_sample_date,
      name == "usgs_so4_shallow" ~ usgs_so4_shallow_sample_date,
      name == "usace_so4_shallow" ~ usace_so4_shallow_sample_date,
      TRUE ~ as.Date("1789-07-14")
    ),
    source = case_when(
      name == "NLA17_SO4" ~ "NLA17",
      name == "NLA22_SO4" ~ "NLA22",
      name == "lagos_so4_shallow" ~ "lagos",
      name == "usgs_so4_shallow" ~ "usgs",
      name == "usace_so4_shallow" ~ "USACE",
      TRUE ~ "Gandalf"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
  select(lake_id, SuRGE_sample_date, source, value, sample_date) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  bind_rows(
    tribble(~lake_id, ~SuRGE_sample_date, ~source, ~value, ~sample_date,
            1002,  as.Date("2016-06-07"),  "Leslie & Lyons (2013)", 
            52.8, as.Date("2011-07-27"),
            204, as.Date("2020-07-27"),  "Ohio Div. of Wildlife", 
            22.9, as.Date("2024-08-14"))
  ) %>%
  arrange(lake_id, source, sample_date) %>% 
  kableExtra::kable(caption = "Table 3. NLA, LAGOS, USACE, and USGS SO4 data for missing lakes") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>%
  collapse_rows(columns = c(1:2)) 

```

Another possibility is to estimate sulfate based on conductivity. The relationship is pretty good in Northern Appalachians, Northern Plains, and Upper Midwest. Northern Plains lake 75 (Freeman Lake) is an outlier with exceptionally high SO4 given the conductivity. This lake is known to be weird; for example, nitrate is 30 mg/l! 

We could estimate sulfate from conductivity for the 10 Northern Appalachian and 2 Upper Midwest lakes for which it is missing.
```{r so4_by_eco, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
dat_raw %>% 
  filter(is.na(so4_shallow)) %>% 
  distinct(lake_id, ag_eco9_nm) %>%
  {table(.$ag_eco9_nm)} %>%
    kableExtra::kable(caption = "Number of lakes with missing sulfate by ecoregion") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

```

```{r so4_cond_plot, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
{dat_raw %>%
    filter(!is.na(ag_eco9_nm)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(
      sp_cond_shallow, so4_shallow, 
      text = paste("SuRGE lake_id:", lake_id))) +
    geom_point() +
    facet_wrap(~ag_eco9_nm, scales = "free") +
    theme(panel.spacing.y = unit(1.5, "cm"))} %>% 
  ggplotly(tooltip = "text")
```

## TP
We are missing TP measurements for `r dat_raw %>% filter(is.na(tp_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` SuRGE lakes (aside from visit 1 to lakes 250 and 281 where the samples were lost in mail).

## TN
We are missing TN measurements for `r dat_raw %>% filter(is.na(tn_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` SuRGE lakes. NLA contains TN observations for `r if(dat_raw %>% filter(is.na(tn_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1) & (!is.na(nla17_ntl) | !is.na(nla22_ntl))) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow() == 0) {print("none")} else {dat_raw %>% filter(is.na(tn_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1) & (!is.na(nla17_ntl) | !is.na(nla22_ntl))) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()}` of these lakes. LAGOS contains TN for 
`r dat_lagos %>% filter(is.na(tn_shallow) & (!is.na(lagos_tn_shallow))) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` of these lakes.

The NLA comparison with TN is pretty good. Also, the 2 lakes with NLA17 and NLA22 observations agree pretty well (Table 2). I think we can imput the missing SuRGE data with the NLA numbers, especially the 2 NLA22 lakes.

## DOC
We are missing DOC measurements for `r dat_raw %>% filter(is.na(doc_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` SuRGE lakes. NLA contains DOC observations for `r if(dat_raw %>% filter(is.na(doc_shallow) & (!is.na(nla17_doc) | !is.na(nla22_doc))) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow() == 0) {print("none")} else {dat_raw %>% filter(is.na(doc_shallow) & (!is.na(nla17_doc) | !is.na(nla22_doc))) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()}` of these lakes, LAGOS contains data for 
`r dat_lagos %>% filter(is.na(doc_shallow) & (!is.na(lagos_doc_shallow))) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` of these lakes, aquamatch contains data for. `r dat_aquamatch %>% filter(is.na(doc_shallow) & (!is.na(aquamatch_doc_shallow)) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()`, the USGS has DOC for `r dat_usgs_chem %>% filter(is.na(doc_shallow) & (!is.na(usgs_doc_shallow)) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()`, and `r dat_usace_chem %>% filter(is.na(doc_shallow) & (!is.na(usace_doc_shallow)) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` have USACE data. Williamson et al. (2023) contains DOC data for 8 of these lakes. Observation dates range from 2006 - 2020, including a sample collected from Acton Lake on day of SuRGE sampling.

Pretty good concurence between NLA and SuRGE DOC, a bit weaker with LAGOS, but look at the data in table 3. Very good concurence between repeat measurements at one lake, even across multiple years. I think we can impute the missing DOC using NLA, LAGOS, and aquamatch. These 3 datasets provide matches to 51 of the missing lakes.

The only DOC data available for seven of the lakes are from aquamatch observations in the late 1970s. The 1970's data matches contemporay observations fairly well in a few of the other lakes (e.g. 1026, 1019, 1011) so maybe these old data are OK, but more recent observations would be preferable.

Chris Nietch measured a TOC value of 6.72 on 2016-08-04, just 3 days after the SuRGE sampling.

Williamson, C.E. 2023. Limnological data from nearly 400 lakes across the Americas and New Zealand with a focus on vertical profiles of temperature, UV radiation, and optical properties ver 5. Environmental Data Initiative. https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/40bb7dc870814ae90437875c506527bf (Accessed 2025-09-18).

```{r doc_table, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

left_join(
  dat_raw %>% 
    select(lake_id, visit, sample_start, 
           doc_shallow, nla17_doc, nla22_doc) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    filter(
      is.na(doc_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)
    ) %>%
    select(-visit),
  dat_lagos %>% 
    select(lake_id, sample_date, lagos_doc_shallow) %>%
    rename(lagos_sample_date = sample_date) %>%
    filter(!is.na(lagos_doc_shallow))
) %>%
  left_join(
    dat_aquamatch %>%
      filter(!is.na(aquamatch_doc_shallow)) %>%
      select(lake_id, activity_start_date, aquamatch_doc_shallow) %>%
      rename(aquamatch_sample_date = activity_start_date) %>%
      distinct()
  ) %>%
  rename(surge_sample_date = sample_start) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(lagos_doc_shallow) | 
      !is.na(aquamatch_doc_shallow) | 
      !is.na(nla17_doc) | 
      !is.na(nla22_doc)
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    dat_williamson_doc %>%
      select(
        lake_id, williamson_doc_shallow_sample_date,
        williamson_doc_shallow
      ) %>%
      distinct()
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    dat_usgs_chem %>%
      select(lake_id, usgs_doc_shallow_sample_date, usgs_doc_shallow) %>%
      distinct()
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    dat_usace_chem %>%
      select(lake_id, usace_doc_shallow_sample_date, usace_doc_shallow) %>%
      distinct()
  ) %>%
  select(-doc_shallow) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(lake_id, contains("date"))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sample_date = case_when(
      name == "nla17_doc" ~ as.Date("2017-01-01"),
      name == "nla22_doc" ~ as.Date("2022-01-01"),
      name == "lagos_doc_shallow" ~ lagos_sample_date,
      name == "williamson_doc_shallow" ~ williamson_doc_shallow_sample_date,
      name == "aquamatch_doc_shallow" ~ aquamatch_sample_date,
      name == "usgs_doc_shallow" ~ usgs_doc_shallow_sample_date,
      name == "usace_doc_shallow" ~ usace_doc_shallow_sample_date,
      TRUE ~ as.Date("1789-07-14")
    ),
    source = case_when(
      name == "nla17_doc" ~ "NLA17",
      name == "nla22_doc" ~ "NLA22",
      name == "lagos_doc_shallow" ~ "lagos",
      name == "williamson_doc_shallow" ~ "williamson",
      name == "aquamatch_doc_shallow" ~ "aquamatch",
      name == "usgs_doc_shallow" ~ "usgs",
      name == "usace_doc_shallow" ~ "USACE",
      TRUE ~ "Gandalf"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
  select(lake_id, surge_sample_date, source, value, sample_date) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(lake_id, source, sample_date) %>% 
  # enforce 2 decimal points for DOC concentration
  mutate(
    value = formatC(
      value, digits = 2, format = "f", drop0trailing = FALSE
      )
    ) %>%
  kableExtra::kable(caption = "Table 3. NLA, LAGOS, USGS, Williamson, USACE, and aquamatch DOC data for missing lakes") %>% 
  column_spec(1, bold = T) %>%
  kable_styling("hover", full_width = FALSE) %>%
  collapse_rows(columns = 1:2)

```

```{r cond_plot, echo=FALSE}
                   "LAGOS sample date:", sample_date),
      color = as.factor(lake_id)
    )
    ) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    ggtitle("sp_cond") +
    xlab("LAGOS sp_cond") +
    ylab("SuRGE sp_cond")} %>%
  ggplotly(tooltip = "text")
```

## Put it all together
The code below replaces missing values with those from the dataset discussed above (including chl a). Preference is given to values from the same year as the SuRGE sampling, else we use the mean of all available data. Aquamatch values from earlier than 2009 are omitted.


```{r impute, echo=FALSE, message = FALSE}
 # IMPUTE TN-----
  # missing values are from 2022 SuRGE sampling. Replace with
  # NLA22 when available, else NLA17.
  dat_impute <- 
    dat_raw %>%
    mutate(tn_shallow = case_when(
      is.na(tn_shallow) & !is.na(nla22_ntl) ~ nla22_ntl,
      is.na(tn_shallow) & is.na(nla22_ntl) & !is.na(nla17_ntl) ~ nla17_ntl,
      TRUE ~ tn_shallow
    ))
  
  # IMPUTE CHLA----
  # Acton Lake (1001) from Vanni's EDI repo
  # https://portal.edirepository.org/nis/mapbrowse?packageid=edi.256.3
  # input_data/external_data/ActonLakeIntegrated.csv

  dat_impute <- 
    dat_impute %>%
    mutate(chla_lab_shallow = case_when(
      # Acton Lake. 28.98 ug/L from Vanni for 5/31/2016
      lake_id == 1001 ~ 28.98,
      
      # Burr Oak from Tanner Williamson (input_data/external_data/Burr Oak chl data.csv)
      # on 2016-07-16 and 2016-07-23
      # Williamson, T. J. (2020). A multi-scale approach to understanding 
      # how environmental variability modulates structure and function in
      # reservoir ecosystems [Doctoral dissertation, Miami University].
      # OhioLINK Electronic Theses and Dissertations Center.
      # http://rave.ohiolink.edu/etdc/view?acc_num=miami1595521238756147
      lake_id == 1007 ~ mean(23.65, 34.45, 27.70, 10.10, 13.20, 7.50,
                             47.10, 50.05, 32.85, 22.50, 31.90, 28.50),
      
      # Beavercreek Upground Reservoir (204) on 2024-08-14
      # email from Scott Jacobs 9/11/2025
      lake_id == 204 ~ 8.12,
      TRUE ~ chla_lab_shallow
    )) %>%
  left_join(
    # Need to add the single estimate for Beaver Upground
    # provided by Ohio Division of Wildlife (ODOW). Creating
    # a small df to contain value that will be merged with greater
    # df. Then chla_lab_shallow will remain NA, but will be
    # populated with mean of all available value (ODOW and NLA)
    dat_impute %>%
      filter(lake_id == 204) %>%
      select(lake_id, site_id, visit) %>%
      mutate(odow_chla_shallow = 8.12)
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    dat_lagos %>%
      select(lake_id, lagos_chla_shallow) %>%
      distinct() %>%
      # exclude missing observations
      filter(!is.na(lagos_chla_shallow)) %>%
      # mean by lake
      group_by(lake_id) %>%
      summarize(lagos_chla_shallow = mean(lagos_chla_shallow))
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    dat_aquamatch %>%
      select(lake_id, aquamatch_chla_shallow) %>%
      distinct() %>%
      # exclude missing observations
      filter(!is.na(aquamatch_chla_shallow)) %>%
      # mean by lake
      group_by(lake_id) %>%
      summarize(aquamatch_chla_shallow = mean(aquamatch_chla_shallow))
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    dat_usgs_chla %>%
      select(lake_id, usgs_chla_lab_shallow) %>%
      distinct() %>%
      # exclude missing observations
      filter(!is.na(usgs_chla_lab_shallow)) %>%
      # mean by lake
      group_by(lake_id) %>%
      summarize(usgs_chla_shallow = mean(usgs_chla_lab_shallow))
  ) %>%
   # replace missing value with mean nla17, nla22, lagos, usgs, odow 
    # this is a rowwise operation
    rowwise() %>% 
    mutate(
      chla_lab_shallow = case_when(
        is.na(chla_lab_shallow) ~ mean(
          c(nla17_chla, nla22_chla, odow_chla_shallow,
            lagos_chla_shallow, aquamatch_chla_shallow,
            usgs_chla_shallow),
          na.rm = TRUE
        ), # close mean
        TRUE ~ chla_lab_shallow)
    ) %>%
    ungroup %>% # remove rowwise
    select(-odow_chla_shallow, -lagos_chla_shallow, 
           -aquamatch_chla_shallow, -usgs_chla_shallow)

  
  # IMPUTE SULFATE----
  # 1. Create so4 ~ cond model for Northern Appalachians.
  #    Model should be built with original observations, not imputed values.
  # 2. Impute missing values with NLA, LAGOS, USGS data to the maximum extent.
  # 3. Use model to impute remaining missing values for the two ecoregions.
  #    See nla_chem_comparison_report.Rmd for details.
  
  ## Define Models----
  so4_model_nap <- lm(so4_shallow ~ sp_cond_shallow, 
                      data = dat_raw %>%  
                        filter(
                          ag_eco9_nm == "Northern Appalachians"
                        )
  )

  
  ## Impute with lagos and/or NLA----
  # none of the lagos or NLA data are from same year as SuRGE
  # observations, so just use mean
  dat_impute <- left_join(
    # 1st df
    dat_impute,
    # bring in lagos data
    dat_lagos %>%
      select(
        lake_id, lagos_so4_shallow
      ) %>%
      distinct() %>%
      # exclude missing observations
      filter(!is.na(lagos_so4_shallow)) %>%
      # mean by lake
      group_by(lake_id) %>%
      summarize(lagos_so4_shallow = mean(lagos_so4_shallow))
  ) %>%
  left_join(
     # Need to add the single estimate for Beaver Upground
    # provided by Ohio Division of Wildlife (ODOW). Creating
    # a small df to contain value that will be merged with greater
    # df. Then so4_shallow will remain NA, but will be
    # populated with mean of all available value (ODOW and NLA)
    dat_impute %>%
      filter(lake_id == 204) %>%
      select(lake_id, site_id, visit) %>%
      mutate(odow_so4_shallow = 22.9)
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    # Need to add the single estimate for Alum Cr. found in 
    # Leslie and Lyons (2013). Creating a small df to contain value
    # that will be merged with greater df. Then so4_shallow will 
    # remain NA, but will be populated with mean of all available values
    # (Leslie and Lyons, USGS)
    dat_impute %>%
      filter(lake_id == 1002) %>%
      select(lake_id, site_id, visit) %>%
      mutate(leslie_lyons_so4_shallow = 52.8)
  ) %>%
  left_join(
   dat_usgs_chem %>%
      select(lake_id, usgs_so4_shallow) %>%
      distinct() %>%
      # exclude missing observations
      filter(!is.na(usgs_so4_shallow)) %>%
      # mean by lake
      group_by(lake_id) %>%
      summarize(usgs_so4_shallow = mean(usgs_so4_shallow)) 
  ) %>%
  left_join(
   dat_usace_chem %>%
      select(lake_id, usace_so4_shallow) %>%
      distinct() %>%
      # exclude missing observations
      filter(!is.na(usace_so4_shallow)) %>%
      # mean by lake
      group_by(lake_id) %>%
      summarize(usace_so4_shallow = mean(usace_so4_shallow)) 
  ) %>%
    # replace missing value with mean of all available data
    # this is a rowwise operation
    rowwise() %>% 
    mutate(
      so4_shallow = case_when(
        is.na(so4_shallow) ~ mean(
          c(nla17_sulfate, nla22_sulfate, lagos_so4_shallow,
            usgs_so4_shallow, odow_so4_shallow, leslie_lyons_so4_shallow,
            usace_so4_shallow),
          na.rm = TRUE
        ), # close mean
        TRUE ~ so4_shallow
      )
    ) %>%
    ungroup %>% # remove rowwise
    select(-lagos_so4_shallow, -usgs_so4_shallow, 
           -odow_so4_shallow, -leslie_lyons_so4_shallow,
           -usace_so4_shallow)
  
  
  ## Impute with model----
  ### Predict missing values for NAP
  pred_so4_nap <- predict(so4_model_nap,
                          newdata = dat_impute %>%
                            filter(
                              ag_eco9_nm == "Northern Appalachians",
                              is.na(so4_shallow) # missing so4
                            )
  ) %>%
    as_tibble() %>% # to tibble
    rename(so4_shallow_predicted = value) %>% # rename parameter
    # bind with unique identifiers
    bind_cols(.,
              dat_impute %>%
                filter(
                  ag_eco9_nm == "Northern Appalachians",
                  is.na(so4_shallow)
                ) %>%
                select(lake_id, site_id, visit)
    )
  
  ### Join predicted data into main dataframe
  dat_impute <- dat_impute %>%
    left_join(pred_so4_nap) %>% # join predictions
    mutate(
      so4_shallow = coalesce( # replace missing with predicted values
        so4_shallow, 
        so4_shallow_predicted
        )
      ) %>%
    select(-so4_shallow_predicted) # remove predictions
  
  # IMPUTE DOC----
  dat_impute <- left_join(
    # 1st df
    dat_impute,
    # join aquamatch data!
    dat_aquamatch %>%
      select(lake_id, activity_start_date, aquamatch_doc_shallow) %>%
      distinct() %>%
      # exclude lake 83 values not wanted. Remaining values
      # are temporally matched (2020-07-27, 2020-08-28) to surge
      # sampling date (2020-08-10)
      filter(
        !(lake_id == 83 & 
            (activity_start_date <= as.Date("2020-06-25") | 
               activity_start_date >= as.Date("2020-09-23")))
      ) %>% # close filter
      # Omit observations from 1970s (all others are > 2009-01-01)
      filter(
        activity_start_date > as.Date("2009-01-01")
      ) %>%
      # calculate mean by lake (collapse time series into one value)
      group_by(lake_id) %>%
      summarize(
        aquamatch_doc_shallow = mean(aquamatch_doc_shallow, na.rm = TRUE)
      ) %>%
      filter(!is.na(aquamatch_doc_shallow), !is.nan(aquamatch_doc_shallow))
  ) %>% # close left_join
    left_join(
      # join lagos data
      dat_lagos %>%
        select(
          lake_id, lagos_doc_shallow
        ) %>%
        distinct() %>%
        # exclude missing observations
        filter(!is.na(lagos_doc_shallow)) %>%
        # mean by lake
        group_by(lake_id) %>%
        summarize(lagos_doc_shallow = mean(lagos_doc_shallow))
    ) %>% # close second join
    left_join(
      # Williamson, C.E. 2023. Limnological data from nearly 400 lakes across
      # the Americas and New Zealand with a focus on vertical profiles of
      # temperature, UV radiation, and optical properties ver 5. Environmental
      # Data Initiative.
      # https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/40bb7dc870814ae90437875c506527bf
      # (Accessed 2025-09-18).
      williamson_doc %>%
        select(
          lake_id, williamson_doc_shallow
        ) %>%
        distinct() %>%
        # exclude missing observations
        filter(!is.na(williamson_doc_shallow)) %>%
        # mean by lake
        group_by(lake_id) %>%
        summarize(williamson_doc_shallow = mean(williamson_doc_shallow))
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      # join lagos data
      usgs_chem %>%
        select(
          lake_id, usgs_doc_shallow
        ) %>%
        distinct() %>%
        # exclude missing observations
        filter(!is.na(usgs_doc_shallow)) %>%
        # mean by lake
        group_by(lake_id) %>%
        summarize(usgs_doc_shallow = mean(usgs_doc_shallow))
    ) %>%
        left_join(
      # join usace data
      usace_chem %>%
        select(
          lake_id, usace_doc_shallow
        ) %>%
        distinct() %>%
        # exclude missing observations
        filter(!is.na(usace_doc_shallow)) %>%
        # mean by lake
        group_by(lake_id) %>%
        summarize(usace_doc_shallow = mean(usace_doc_shallow))
    ) %>%
    # replace missing value with mean of all available data
    # this is a rowwise operation
    rowwise() %>% 
    mutate(
      doc_shallow = case_when(
        lake_id == 83 ~ aquamatch_doc_shallow, # sampling date match
        is.na(doc_shallow) ~ mean(
          c(nla17_doc, nla22_doc, lagos_doc_shallow, 
            aquamatch_doc_shallow, williamson_doc_shallow,
            usgs_doc_shallow, usace_doc_shallow),
          na.rm = TRUE
        ), # close mean
        TRUE ~ doc_shallow
      )
    ) %>%
    ungroup %>% # remove rowwise
    select(-lagos_doc_shallow, -aquamatch_doc_shallow,
           -williamson_doc_shallow, -usgs_doc_shallow,
           -usace_doc_shallow)


```



## Missing data
We are missing extraction-based chlorophyll a measurements for `r dat_impute %>% filter(is.na(chla_lab_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` SuRGE lakes (mostly 2016 lakes).

We are missing sulfate data for `r dat_impute %>% filter(is.na(so4_shallow)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` SuRGE lakes.

We are missing TN measurements for `r dat_impute %>% filter(is.na(tn_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` SuRGE lakes.

We are missing DOC measurements for `r dat_impute %>% filter(is.na(doc_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` SuRGE lakes.
